metadata.title: Attitudes towards science in higher education: Validation of questionnaire among science teacher candidates and engineering students in Indonesia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study collected questionnaire responses from 296 second-year science teacher candidates and engineering students in Central Java, Indonesia, using cluster random sampling across three universities. The analysis used confirmatory factor analysis (CFA with WLSMV), Rasch analysis, and reliability checks, and then compared group differences using logit scores derived from Rasch modeling. The manuscript does not report the use of any complex survey design weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate weights, and the data are not described as an international large-scale assessment microdata file requiring PV-based weighting. Because the dependent variables are psychometric/attitudinal constructs (latent dimensions and Rasch logit measures) rather than ILSA achievement PVs, the weighting guidance is limited to the described university-based sampling; results should be interpreted as validation and group-comparison evidence for this sampled population rather than population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the study does not use ILSA-style cognitive achievement scales with PVs; instead, it validates an attitude questionnaire using CFA and Rasch analysis and reports Rasch logit measures for attitude dimensions. Missing-data handling is not reported because the paper focuses on instrument validation and does not describe any explicit missing-response exclusion or imputation procedure for the questionnaire items.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were 296 second-year undergraduate students from three universities in Central Java, Indonesia. The sample comprised science teacher candidates (56.08%) and engineering students (43.92%) and was selected using cluster random sampling. The manuscript does not report additional item-level or case-level exclusions (e.g., minimum response thresholds, missing-item rules) beyond voluntary completion of the online questionnaire.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This Heliyon study validates an Indonesian version of the Attitude Towards Science Questionnaire (ATSQ) for higher-education students (second-year science teacher candidates and food engineering students) using psychometric methods rather than predictive machine learning. The sample includes 296 students from three universities in Central Java, Indonesia. Construct validity was evaluated with CFA (WLSMV) reporting CMIN/df = 2.61, CFI = 0.98, TLI = 0.98, RMSEA = 0.07, and SRMR = 0.04, and Rasch analysis showed good item fit (infit MNSQ minfit ≈ 0.99; outfit MNSQ moutfit ≈ 0.98) with acceptable dimensionality (average variance explained ≥ 30%). Reliability was high overall (Cronbach alpha = 0.95; McDonald omega = 0.95), while the anxiety/difficulty dimension showed lower item reliability (≈ 0.38). Group comparisons indicated no significant differences between science teacher candidates and engineering students across the four attitude dimensions and total attitude, with moderate overall attitude levels (mean ≈ 0.54 logit). Limitations include lack of reported missing-data handling and the absence of ML prediction performance metrics; findings support questionnaire validity and descriptive group patterns within this sampled context. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is an instrument validation and group-comparison study using CFA and Rasch/Rasch-based psychometrics, not an empirical ML prediction study. Consequently, there are no ILSA program/cycle PV-based achievement outcomes, no ML algorithms, and no predictive performance metrics to populate main_findings. The extraction therefore leaves main_findings empty and sets ml_techniques to an empty list, while still capturing the sample and psychometric results in outcome_summary.
